claim: A barred strongroom in a shop's back wall (a recess a step up at the room's own floor and ceiling, a blocking masked grille, the owner's grate 463, a lit lower room behind) reads as a jail cell until goods stand inside it; then it is 'a shop's secure stock'. It is a detail, not depth: it moved none of the per-interior measures that separate a flat interior from the campaign's, and a cage nothing meets and nobody can open reads as decoration.
evidence: projects/blood-city/experiments/pledge-room/what-if.png, five unlabelled sets; the pawn shop before and after: floor heights 5 and 5, ceiling heights 3 and 4, wall tiles 10 and 13, shade spread 17 and 18 (tools/city_profile.py --interiors); tests/test_whatif.py PledgeRoomTests, GrilleTests
use: Build it with bloodmap.glass.grille and stock it; piercing a wall changes which wall is the longest solid one, so anything placed by that rule (the shop's sign) moves.
